_doc: The S-13 client-repoint inventory: every tracked file carrying an address that MOVES in the
generation-1 -> generation-2 cutover, and what each one is.
This file is DATA for scripts/check-cutover-consumers.sh, which fails when the tree and this
manifest disagree in either direction. It exists because the cutover's realistic failure mode is
not repointing the wrong address - it is repointing 22 of the 25 files in the repoint group and
shipping the other 3 still aimed at generation 1, silently. Those counts are derived from the
`consumers` list below by the classes in _consumerClassDoc; do not restate them from memory.
Six addresses are SUPERSEDED; that is not the same as six being CLEARED TO MOVE. Each entry
carries a `semanticEquivalence` verdict, because an address may be repointed only when the
successor answers THE SAME QUESTION FOR THE SAME INPUTS - a matching selector is not evidence of
that. IssuerRegistry currently fails that condition on every axis and is BLOCKED.
Addresses are matched in FULL (40 hex digits) and CASE-INSENSITIVELY. Both halves are load-bearing;
see docs/CLIENT_REPOINT.md for the two ways an 8-hex case-sensitive grep gets this wrong.
generation2 is null for every entry because nothing is deployed. S-13 repoints; S-14 deploys.
A placeholder here would be the invented data this fleet forbids.

movingAddresses.supersededBy: SPLITS BY CALLER ROLE - see supersededBy on each consumer entry
movingAddresses.semanticEquivalence: VERIFIED per role. rootIssuer/isClone on CloneProvenanceRouter answer the same questions with the same arguments and no caller scoping (the router's isClone is deliberately WIDER - true for a clone of any registered generation - which is the question a post-cutover provenance check must ask). predictIssuer/createIssuer on DogTagIssuerFactoryV2 are the same selectors on the same arguments.
note: THE ONLY MOVING ADDRESS THAT DOES NOT HAVE ONE TARGET. It splits by what the caller does with
it, and the two halves move in OPPOSITE directions - so a per-consumer `supersededBy` overrides
this entry wherever the answer is not the reader default.
READER (resolves the write-once rootIssuer[R], or asks isClone) -> CloneProvenanceRouter, which
answers across BOTH generations oldest-first. Point a reader at DogTagIssuerFactoryV2 and every
one of the 19 historical roots resolves to address(0), surfacing as an indeterminate
issuer-whitelist pillar rather than an error. The router's isClone is also DELIBERATELY wider -
true for a clone of any registered generation - which is the question a post-cutover provenance
check must ask; a generation-1-only answer reports every genuine generation-2 clone as
NotFactoryDeployed.
WRITER (predictIssuer / createIssuer calldata) -> DogTagIssuerFactoryV2. The router deploys
nothing and owns nothing.
EMITTER ALLOWLIST (the indexer's INDEXER_GENERATIONS.factory) -> DogTagIssuerFactoryV2, and as an
APPEND beside generation 1 rather than a swap. That list is keyed by who SIGNED a log, and the
router emits nothing, so a router address there would silently match no event ever.

movingAddresses.supersededBy: BLOCKED - no consumer of this address may be repointed at C-9. See note.
movingAddresses.repointStep: BLOCKED until the isRecognizedIssuer migration (docs/ISSUER_V2_OWNERSHIP.md section 8)
movingAddresses.semanticEquivalence: FAILS on the record-type key shape, HOLDS on the VERIFY key shape - and one env variable feeds both
note: THIS ENTRY IS THE WORKED EXAMPLE OF THE GOVERNING CONDITION (docs/CLIENT_REPOINT.md): the
successor implements the selector and answers, and its answer MEANS SOMETHING ELSE. Two
earlier revisions of this entry each authorized a repoint that breaks the fleet, so read the
whole note before shortening it.
WRITE AXIS - ProviderRegistry implements NEITHER whitelistFor NOR delistFor and has no
fallback, so a variable naming those writes cannot be repointed here at all. admin-api's
grant/revoke console builds that calldata against cfg.issuer_registry_addr and is RETAINED on
the generation-1 registry through C-12. Two reasons, the second outranking the first.
(1) ProviderRegistry.hasRole(WHITELIST_ADMIN, owner) returns true, so governance::dispatch
reads the hosted key as the holder and BROADCASTS a reverting transaction rather than cleanly
proposing - a config error wearing the costume of a chain problem, mid-cutover. (2) C-12's
delisting freeze runs through this same console, and that freeze is the operational
precondition for closing CloneProvenanceRouter's open mirror direction.
READ AXIS - NOT UNIFORM, and this is the half that looked safe. ProviderRegistry.isWhitelistedFor
(ProviderRegistry.sol:787-793) branches on msg.sender: an ATTACHED SERVICE caller gets its own
service grant, and EVERY OTHER caller gets _verifierCapabilities[key][signer] - the orthogonal
VERIFY axis, written only by setVerifierCapability. Every production read is a plain eth_call
with NO `from` set (grep -c '\.from(' over vet/government/admin chain.rs returns 0; packages/ui
readContract passes no account), so msg.sender is the zero address and that second branch
ALWAYS runs. Which branch you land in is invisible from the ABI.
So the answer depends on WHICH KEY the caller passes, not on which service it is:
COMPATIBLE - the VERIFY-key reads. verify_key_from_purpose_word builds
keccak256(abi.encode("VERIFY:", purpose)), byte-identical to ProviderRegistry.verificationKey
(ProviderRegistry.sol:781), so it indexes the very mapping that branch returns. Four sites:
stacks/vet/api/src/routes.rs:1463, stacks/vet/api/src/verify.rs:505,
stacks/government/api/src/routes.rs:1452, stacks/government/api/src/verify.rs:302.
BROKEN - the RECORD-TYPE-key reads. keccak256(recordType) is never a verificationKey output,
so _verifierCapabilities[keccak256(recordType)][signer] is false for EVERY genuine issuer
signer - a definite false, not an error. Seven sites: stacks/vet/api/src/routes.rs:549, :658,
:969, :1258, :1308; stacks/government/api/src/routes.rs:702; and packages/ui's
isWhitelistedFor, whose key is recordTypeKey(...) by construction (contracts.ts).
CONSEQUENCE of repointing anyway. routes.rs:1258 (vet) and routes.rs:702 (government) ARE the
mandatory issuer-whitelist pillar, which treats a definite false as an AUTHENTICITY FAILURE -
so genuine credentials are refused as forged, fleet-wide. vet routes.rs:549 and :658 are the
issuance preflight, so the vet's own whitelisted signer is refused and issuance STOPS. vet
:969/:1308 and the admin/web whitelist viewer render every row false.
WHY THE VARIABLE CANNOT SIMPLY MOVE FOR THE COMPATIBLE HALF: ISSUER_REGISTRY_ADDR is ONE value
read by both key shapes in the SAME process - vet routes.rs:1463 (VERIFY key) and :549
(record-type key) both read st.cfg.issuer_registry_addr. So there is nothing to split at the
config layer, and the whole variable stays on generation 1 until the record-type callers
migrate to the service-scoped isRecognizedIssuer(service, signer) - a DIFFERENT selector with
different arguments, i.e. a code change in five consumers, recorded as a cutover blocker in
docs/ISSUER_V2_OWNERSHIP.md section 8.
DO NOT 'fix' this by leaving the readers on generation 1 and calling it done either: a
generation-2 root then resolves nowhere and the pillar is INDETERMINATE. Both states are
broken, differently, and only the migration closes either.
THE CONTRACT SIDE IS PINNED; THE CONSUMER SIDE IS NOT. contracts/test/ProviderRegistry.t.sol
exercises isWhitelistedFor at BOTH caller contexts - vm.prank affects only the NEXT call, so
the pranked (attached-service, first-branch) cases are :552, :588, :590, :592 and :841, while
:598, :836 and :845 run UNPRANKED at production's zero-address caller. :598 is the exact case
that matters: unpranked, keyed on RECORD_TYPE, asserting false - and :599 immediately asserts
isRecognizedIssuer(service, signer) is TRUE for that same signer. So the suite pins both
halves of the migration, under the inline comment stating the split-BY-QUESTION rule.
THE REAL RESIDUAL GAP is one layer up: nothing anywhere asserts what the CONSUMERS do when
handed that false. The mandatory issuer-whitelist pillar's outcome against ProviderRegistry is
unpinned in every suite - no Rust or TS test references ProviderRegistry at all, and MemChain's
is_whitelisted_for is a flat (registry, recordType, signer) map lookup that cannot model the
msg.sender branch, so the case is not merely unwritten but unrepresentable in the hermetic
fakes without a new one. Closing it belongs with the isRecognizedIssuer migration, which is the
change that gives those consumers something correct to assert against.
Generation-1 clones keep reading the generation-1 registry on-chain regardless - a clone pins
its registry at initialize with no setter - so nothing above affects on-chain generation-1
issuance, which stops only at the C-12 freeze.
movingAddresses.supersededByVerifyKeyReaders: ProviderRegistry - semantically equivalent, but UNREACHABLE alone: the same env variable also serves the record-type readers below
movingAddresses.supersededByEmitterAllowlist: ProviderRegistry, APPENDED beside generation 1 in INDEXER_GENERATIONS.issuerRegistry - but NOT sufficient on its own. That member is an EMITTER address, so its question is 'which events does it emit', and ProviderRegistry emits NEITHER Whitelisted NOR Delisted (it emits IssuanceCapabilitySet / VerifierCapabilitySet - different names, topic0 and argument shapes). The scanner filters by the Whitelisted/Delisted topic0, so the address alone leaves that generation's whitelist axis permanently dark, failing the same SILENT way a late append does. Pair it with a decoder change or do not append it.
movingAddresses.supersededByRecordTypeKeyReaders: BLOCKED - requires the isRecognizedIssuer(service, signer) migration; ProviderRegistry answers a definite false here
movingAddresses.supersededByWriters: IssuerRegistry (RETAINED through C-12 - ProviderRegistry has no whitelistFor/delistFor)

movingAddresses.semanticEquivalence: UNVERIFIED - the V2 contract is not written, so no question-for-question comparison has been made. Establish it before C-9, not during.
note: Its issuerRegistry / sbt / rootIndex are all immutable, so replacing the authority core forces
this redeploy on its own. C-6 must migrate the VERIFY: relayer capabilities BEFORE any client
is repointed here: restrictToWhitelistedRelayers defaults true, so a client on V2 whose relayer
was not migrated gets !verify-wl on every verification.

movingAddresses.semanticEquivalence: VERIFIED, and enforced STRUCTURALLY. The record is deliberately RENAMED (getDiscoverySet/resolveDiscovery, 10 words vs 8), so a generation-1 client cannot dispatch and misdecode it; getArtifactSet/getActiveArtifactSet keep their selectors because the artifact record is genuinely unchanged. See docs/PROTOCOL_REGISTRY_V2.md.
note: The discovery anchor. Generation 2 publishes under the NEW discovery key dogtag-levelb/2; the
ARTIFACT key stays dogtag-levelb-artifacts/1 because the artifacts are byte-for-byte identical
and a second identity for them would be a falsehood. See docs/PROTOCOL_REGISTRY_V2.md.

movingAddresses.semanticEquivalence: UNVERIFIED. ServiceDomainResolver deliberately does NOT expose domainOf(address) returns (string) - resolveDomain returns a tuple carrying a Disposition, because an empty string was three different facts. That is a CODE change in every consumer, not an address repoint. See docs/SERVICE_DOMAIN_RESOLVER.md.
note: Abandoning the deployed one is free: boundCloneCount() == 0 AND zero logs of any kind at head
303690 on 2026-07-30. Read the log count, not just the counter - setDomainAdmin appoints a key
without writing a binding, so only 'no logs' establishes nothing is stranded.

movingAddresses.semanticEquivalence: NOT APPLICABLE - no consumer calls this address. It is the clone implementation, identified by codehash at factory construction and recorded in the ledger and both mobile bundles.
note: The clone implementation. DogTagIssuerFactoryV2 identifies it EXACTLY, by
impl.codehash == keccak256(type(DogTagIssuerV2).runtimeCode), so an ABI-shaped impostor is
refused at construction. Carried here because both mobile bundles and the ledger record it.

_doNotMoveDoc: Two live addresses are deliberately REUSED by generation 2 and must not appear in any repoint.
Listing them is the point: they look like they should move and they must not.

reason: profileRoot is per-contract and write-once, so a new SBT has no root for any existing tag and
every existing tag would fail the R == profileRoot(dogTagId) binding. Reuse costs nothing:
minting gates on the SBT's own ISSUER_ROLE, not on the issuer registry, so it is independent
of the authority swap. C-10b must grant that role to the generation-2 issuing signers.
The circuit and the ceremony VK are frozen and unchanged by any of this work.

_consumerClassDoc.runtime-constant: A compiled-in or bundled constant that resolves a live address. Repoint at C-9/C-10.
_consumerClassDoc.service-default: A backend's hard-coded fallback for an env var. Repoint at C-9.
_consumerClassDoc.config-template: .env.example - operator-facing template, read by nobody at runtime. Moves with the code per the captain's standing rule.
_consumerClassDoc.operational-script: A demo/e2e shell script that drives the live chain. Repoint at C-9.
_consumerClassDoc.documentation: A live-address table or runbook. Moves with the code.
_consumerClassDoc.historical-ledger: PRESERVE. The deployment record. AGENTS.md: do not rewrite historical records.
_consumerClassDoc.pinned-fixture: PRESERVE. Pinned to a block; the S-12 fork test REFUSES to run if it disagrees with the fork.
_consumerClassDoc.hermetic-fixture: PRESERVE. A MemChain or mocked-network constant that resolves nothing live. Reusing a real address here is cosmetic.
_consumerClassDoc.inventory-manifest: PRESERVE the generation-1 values. This file itself, which records WHAT MOVED and therefore holds every generation-1 address by design. S-14 fills each `generation2` beside its `generation1`; it never replaces one, or the record of what moved from where is lost.

VERIFICATION_REGISTRY_CONSENT_ADDR - the eth_getLogs address for the owner wallet's consent-history scan (src/lib/chain.ts fetchVerifiedLogs). It carried the SUPERSEDED M5 instance while its own comment called it live, so the scan queried a dead contract and rendered 'no consent history' for absent evidence. That is why retiredAddresses exists: grepping the CURRENT value could never have found it.
INDEXER_GENERATIONS defaults. Must accept the generation-2 triple BEFORE generation 2 emits: the anti-spoof gate drops unrecognised emitters SILENTLY.
consumers.supersededBy: DogTagIssuerFactoryV2 - DEFAULT_FACTORY seeds the same emitter allowlist as the env above.

TWO divergences. (1) FACTORY_ADDR -> DogTagIssuerFactoryV2, not the router: it is a WRITE target (predictIssuer + createIssuer calldata), and verified no admin caller reads root_issuer or is_clone through cfg.factory_addr. (2) ISSUER_REGISTRY_ADDR -> RETAINED on the generation-1 IssuerRegistry through C-12, because ProviderRegistry implements no whitelistFor/delistFor and no fallback. This is the only .env.example where ISSUER_REGISTRY_ADDR names a WRITE path - but do not read that as the others moving: every OTHER stack's copy is blocked too, on the separate read-axis ground in the IssuerRegistry note. No consumer of that variable moves at C-9.
DogTagIssuerFactoryV2, APPENDED as a second INDEXER_GENERATIONS object rather than swapped - generation 1 keeps its object or its whole history leaves the oversight feed.

Declared rather than skipped. An implicit self-exemption is a silent hole in the one check that exists to find silent holes - and this entry was added only because the gate flagged its own manifest the moment it became tracked. Until then the check was passing because git grep cannot see an untracked file, which is a check passing by not running.

_retiredAddressDoc: Addresses this repo has ALREADY superseded. They need their own check because the inventory above
is derived by grepping the CURRENT generation-1 value, which is structurally blind to a consumer
still holding an older one - such a file carries no moving address at all, so it looks clean.
The blind spot was live rather than theoretical: stacks/owner/web/src/lib/config.ts pinned the M5
VerificationRegistryConsent while its own comment called it the live one, so the owner wallet's
consent history scanned a dead contract and rendered 'no consent history'. Absence of evidence
presented as evidence of absence - this repo's own standing defect class, on a user-facing surface.
A retired address appears legitimately in many places, so this uses the SAME declared-allowlist
discipline as the inventory rather than a blanket ban: an UNDECLARED carrier is an error, and a
declared carrier that no longer holds it is only a note. The allowlist is scoped PER ADDRESS, so a
file cleared to carry one is not thereby cleared to carry another. This manifest declares ITSELF,
for the same reason the inventory does - an implicit self-exemption is a hole in the one check

_elidedDoc: Files that reference a moving address ONLY in elided prose form (0xED20269E...), so a full-address
grep cannot see them. They still need a human edit at cutover. They are listed rather than matched
because widening the grep to 8-hex prefixes produces false positives - see docs/CLIENT_REPOINT.md.
